title: Amazon: attackers used the Cairn AI tool to exploit a MONAI Label zero-day and take over a server, BleepingComputer reports
date_note: Date of BleepingComputer's report; it says the attacks ran 8 to 10 September 2026 and the maintainers released a security update on 18 November.
org: East Asian educational institutions (MONAI Label users)
geo_basis: region named by the source: mainly East Asian educational institutions outside China; no pin for a single organisation
summary: Amazon found AI agents running the Cairn tool exploiting a path traversal zero-day in MONAI Label, a medical imaging application, within 11 minutes of mapping its API, BleepingComputer reports. They gained root on a server; the operator then pointed them at a second university network. Amazon attributes it to a Chinese-nexus actor with moderate confidence. BleepingComputer says an update followed on 18 November; Startup Fortune, relaying SecurityWeek, says no fixed release exists yet.
plain: Amazon says attackers used an autonomous AI tool to find and exploit a flaw in medical imaging software and take over a university server. Reports differ on whether a fixed release is out yet.
exec: AI agents were reported to go from mapping an API to exploiting a flaw in 11 minutes; organisations running MONAI Label should follow the maintainers' advisory.
action: If you run MONAI Label, follow the maintainers' advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94, which BleepingComputer links as the security update; Startup Fortune reports no fixed release yet.

attribution.note: moderate confidence, from prompt language, activity timestamps and target choice, as relayed by BleepingComputer

validation.note: BleepingComputer and The Record (independent publishers) both relay Amazon's finding of a path traversal zero-day in a medical imaging application, used against a university and then a second one, since fixed by the maintainers. The Record does not name MONAI Label or give a confidence level; both rely on Amazon, whose own report was not read. Follow-up 23 Nov: Startup Fortune (22 Nov, relaying SecurityWeek and The Hacker News) says the fix is merged in source but not in a release, against BleepingComputer's 18 November security update; the GitHub advisory returned 403 and Amazon's post did not load, so both accounts are given.

review.note: Compared 8-10 Sept dates, 11 minutes, root access, proxy, moderate-confidence Chinese-nexus attribution, 18 Nov update, MONAI Label, East Asia targets against BleepingComputer and The Record
